title: Give, and it will be given (Luke 6:27–38)
hookLine: good measure, pressed down, shaken together, running over

cards: At a grain market, you hold out your measure, a basket or a jar. A stingy seller fills it loosely, full of air pockets, and levels it off flat.

A generous one pours the grain in, presses it down with his hand, shakes the container so it settles, pours in more, and keeps going until it's heaped and spilling over the sides, and you hold out the fold of your robe to catch the rest.
That's the picture Jesus ends this teaching with. But first, he says some very hard things.

teach.b: Still on the level place, in the King James words: "Love your enemies, do good to them which hate you, Bless them that curse you, and pray for them which despitefully use you." Turn the other cheek.
Give to everyone who asks. Lend, hoping for nothing back. And the line now called the Golden Rule: "as ye would that men should do to you, do ye also to them likewise."

teach.h: BE YE MERCIFUL, AS YOUR FATHER.
teach.b: Then the center of it all: "Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful." Mercy is the measure.

teach.h: GOOD MEASURE, PRESSED DOWN, RUNNING OVER.
teach.b: And the picture from the market: "Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom." Bosom here isn't your chest.

The Greek word, kolpos, can mean the lap or the fold of a robe, which could hold grain like a pouch. A lap overflowing. Then the hinge: "For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again."
Mete means to measure out. This isn't a get-rich promise; a few lines earlier, Jesus told people to lend, hoping for nothing again.
The measure is about mercy: judge not, condemn not, forgive, give, and the same measure comes back.

teach.h: GIVE, AND IT SHALL BE GIVEN UNTO YOU.
teach.b: The basket you hold out to others is the basket you're handed. Running over.

how: Christians often read Luke 6:38 as a call to generous giving, alongside the Golden Rule in Luke 6:31.

o: lend only to people who can repay you
share freely, and a full measure comes back
keep careful count of what others owe you

games.q: you're selling grain at the market. a poor customer holds out a basket. how do you fill it?
o: fill it loosely and level it off.
press it down, shake it together, and let it run over.
fill it halfway; business is business.
games.why: Jesus' picture is the heaped measure, pressed and shaken until it spills into the lap. the measure you use is the one that comes back.

practice: Picture your hands as the seller's hands, holding a basket, and think of someone you could give to: money, maybe, or time, praise, patience, a long phone call.
Notice the first instinct to level it off, then picture pressing it down, shaking it together, adding a bit more: a longer visit, a real compliment instead of a quick one.
If you pray, you can ask for open hands; if you don't, simply picture the basket overflowing.

wordCard.voice: Give. Jesus' teaching on the plain: be merciful, give without counting, and what you give comes back pressed down, shaken together and running over.

orig.note: Greek: lap, bosom, the fold of a garment. where the overflowing measure is poured.

carryVoice: Your line: running over. Pressed down, shaken together, spilling into your lap. Day five hundred twenty-four, and counting.
